From 4007844b05815717f522c7ea9914e24ad0ff6c79 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2020 11:31:35 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] soc: mediatek: Check if power domains can be powered on at
 boot time

In the error case, where a power domain cannot be powered on
successfully at boot time (in mtk_register_power_domains),
pm_genpd_init would still be called with is_off=false, and the
system would later try to disable the power domain again, triggering
warnings as disabled clocks are disabled again (and other potential
issues).

Also print a warning splat in that case, as this should never
happen.

Fixes: c84e358718a66f7 ("soc: Mediatek: Add SCPSYS power domain driver")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200928113107.v2.1.I5e6f8c262031d0451fe7241b744f4f3111c1ce71@changeid
Signed-off-by: Matthias Brugger <matthias.bgg@gmail.com>

diff --git a/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c b/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
index f669d3754627..ca75b14931ec 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
@@ -524,6 +524,7 @@ static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		struct scp_domain *scpd = &scp->domains[i];
 		struct generic_pm_domain *genpd = &scpd->genpd;
+		bool on;
 
 		/*
 		 * Initially turn on all domains to make the domains usable
@@ -531,9 +532,9 @@ static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 		 * software.  The unused domains will be switched off during
 		 * late_init time.
 		 */
-		genpd->power_on(genpd);
+		on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
 
-		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
+		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
 	}
 
 	/*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c`**
   - A new boolean variable `on` is introduced to track the success of powering on the power domains.
   - The call to `genpd->power_on(genpd)` is modified to check for errors. If it returns a negative value, a warning is triggered, and `on` is set to false.
   - The `pm_genpd_init` function call is updated to use the value of `on` instead of a hardcoded `false`. This change ensures that the initialization reflects whether the power domain was successfully powered on.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `mtk-scpsys.c` are interrelated as they address a specific issue during the boot process of the power domains. The introduction of the `on` variable allows the code to conditionally initialize the power management domain based on whether the power domain was successfully powered on. This prevents the system from attempting to disable a power domain that failed to power on, which could lead to warnings and other potential issues. The changes ensure that the system behaves correctly during initialization and improves error handling by providing a warning when a power domain cannot be powered on.

Here is the commit message:
soc: mediatek: Check if power domains can be powered on at
 boot time

In the error case, where a power domain cannot be powered on
successfully at boot time (in mtk_register_power_domains),
pm_genpd_init would still be called with is_off=false, and the
system would later try to disable the power domain again, triggering
warnings as disabled clocks are disabled again (and other potential
issues).

Also print a warning splat in that case, as this should never
happen.

Fixes: c84e358718a66f7 ("soc: Mediatek: Add SCPSYS power domain driver")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200928113107.v2.1.I5e6f8c262031d0451fe7241b744f4f3111c1ce71@changeid
Signed-off-by: Matthias Brugger <matthias.bgg@gmail.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the `pm_genpd_init` function is called with `is_off=false` even when a power domain fails to power on during boot. This leads to the system attempting to disable a power domain that was never successfully enabled, resulting in warnings and potential issues with disabled clocks being disabled again.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 				struct scp *scp, int num)
 {
 	struct genpd_onecell_data *pd_data;
 	int i, ret;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		struct scp_domain *scpd = &scp->domains[i];
 		struct generic_pm_domain *genpd = &scpd->genpd;
+		bool on;
 
 		/*
 		 * Initially turn on all domains to make the domains usable
 		 * with !CONFIG_PM and to get the hardware in sync with the
 		 * software.  The unused domains will be switched off during
 		 * late_init time.
 		 */
-		genpd->power_on(genpd);
+		on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
 
-		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
+		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
 	}
 
 	/*
 	 * We are not allowed to fail here since there is no way to unregister
 	 * a power domain. Once registered above we have to keep the domains
 	 * valid.
 	 */
 
 	pd_data = &scp->pd_data;
 
 	ret = of_genpd_add_provider_onecell(pdev->dev.of_node, pd_data);
 	if (ret)
 		dev_err(&pdev->dev, "Failed to add OF provider: %d\n", ret);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
genpd->power_on(genpd);
```
Reason:
The `pm_genpd_init` function is called with `is_off=false` regardless of whether the `power_on` function succeeds or fails. If the power domain fails to power on, the system will later attempt to disable a power domain that was never successfully enabled, leading to warnings and potential issues with disabled clocks being disabled again.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
```
Reason:
The patch checks the return value of `genpd->power_on(genpd)` and sets the `on` variable accordingly. If the power domain fails to power on, `on` will be `false`, and `pm_genpd_init` will be called with `is_off=true`, preventing the system from trying to disable a power domain that was never successfully enabled.
